label: Ancient
description: From the earliest urban civilization of the Indus Valley through the Mauryan, Gupta and post-Gupta periods. This era produced some of India's most enduring sculpture, architecture and mural traditions.

label: Medieval
description: Marked by the rise of regional kingdoms and their distinctive artistic programmes — from Chola bronzes and Dravidian temple architecture to Chandela temples, Mughal painting and Rajput miniature traditions.

label: Modern
description: A period of profound transformation driven by colonial encounter, nationalist movements and the search for an Indian modernity in art. Includes the Bengal School, Company painting and the pioneering generation of Amrita Sher-Gil.

label: Contemporary
description: Post-independence India produced a rich range of art practice: from the Progressive Artists' Group's engagement with international modernism to living folk traditions such as Madhubani and Warli, and globally circulating contemporary art.
